source.title: Ichthyofaunal Community in Dibut River Baler, Aurora
source.citation: Mercader, K., Mora?a, M. L., Belga, A., De Guzman, M., & Bobes, R. (2025). Ichthyofaunal Community in Dibut River Baler, Aurora. Egyptian Journal of Aquatic Biology and Fisheries, 29(3), 173-182. https://doi.org/10.21608/ejabf.2025.426195

stations.reach: lower reach; paper describes freshwater/saltwater meeting

site.coordinateMeaning: Article station coordinates, not exact specimen capture points or reach boundaries; decimals are conversions from the printed DMS values.

methods.sampling: Monthly gill-net sampling at all three stations, reported net size 100 x 1 m and mesh size 14, set about 06:00 and harvested at 18:00 with lunar-phase sampling; field period October 2023 to March 2024.
methods.identification: Authors say specimens were identified using online materials and local guides, and FishBase/IUCN were used for scientific names. The article itself recommends DNA barcoding for further identification work.
methods.scope: The lower reach is described as an estuarine freshwater/saltwater interface; paper reports Station 1 salinity averaging 7.92-18.04 ppt, Station 2 1.73-2.44 ppt, and Station 3 0 ppt. Preserve as reported station measurements, not a mapped salinity boundary.

reportedEvidence.interpretation: The abstract says 22 species; the results and conclusion say 23; Table 1 visibly contains 22 listed taxon rows and its site totals are 13, 12, and 14. Preserve this source conflict; do not select a definitive total.

rights.articleSpecificLicense: No article-specific reuse notice was found in the accessible PDF text or publisher record during this review.
rights.journalLevelMetadata: DOAJ journal metadata lists CC BY-NC-SA, but it is journal-level information last fully reviewed in 2021 and is not treated as a confirmed article-specific grant.
rights.publisherPolicy: The publisher website says article copyright transfers to the journal.
rights.disposition: Rights remain unresolved for Bangwit product or public redistribution; no table rows, figures, or article prose are copied into the research artifact.

issues: Source species count conflicts: abstract 22 versus results/conclusion 23; Table 1 has 22 rows.
The authors recommend DNA barcoding, so source identification is not treated as independently verified here.
Some abstract/table spellings differ, including Planiliza macrolepsis/macrolepis, Mesoprites/Mesopristes cancellatus, and Hypoatherina temmincki/temminckii. Names are not silently corrected.
Gill-net catches and monthly lunar-phase biomass are method-specific historical observations, not current presence, abundance, catchability, legal status, diet, or bait guidance.
The source does not provide an authoritative boundary for freshwater, brackish, or marine sections of the river.
nextStep: Keep as a source and locality lead. Resolve article-level reuse terms and source-name/count conflicts before any table-derived adaptation; Central Luzon remains incomplete.
